The incumbent may be exposed to infected patients and contaminated materials and may be required to don protective clothing in isolation situations, operative/invasive procedures, or home settings. The incumbent must be a mature, flexible, sensible individual capable of working effectively in stressful situations, able to shift priorities based on patient needs. Must complete annual Employee Health requirements, such as annual TB screening or testing, as a condition of employment.

The incumbent who provides care in home settings or other off-site locations may be required to drive and/or ride in GSA-vehicles.

The Inpatient Spinal Cord Injury/Disorder Registered Nurse will function as an integral member of the Spinal Cord Division. These are exciting opportunities to work in a diverse environment.

Position offers opportunities to provide bedside care for acute and chronic disease management, palliative care patients, rehabilitation and complex medical patients.

Grounded in partnerships with more than 20 leading health systems, deep EMR integrations, dedicated medical group, and experience serving a population of more than 100,000 patients, the system learns from real-world care delivery, improving as it scales.

In this role, you will proactively monitor patient data, evaluate clinical information, and deliver timely interventions to promote patient safety and improved health outcomes.

You will work closely with interdisciplinary care teams to reinforce care plans, support medication adherence, close care gaps, and provide patient education that empowers individuals to actively manage their health and chronic conditions.

Licensure Requirements ActiveCompact Multi-State RN license is required Schedule Requirements: This role requires availability Monday - Friday.

Schedule hours are 8 :00 AM to 5:00 PM in Pacific Time What you'll do: Proactively monitor patient vitals, symptoms, and relevant clinical data to identify care gaps and patients who require timely intervention. Develop, implement, and manage individualized care plans aligned with physician recommendations and patient-specific health goals.

Engage with patients via phone and secure messaging to address concerns, manage escalations, and provide empathetic, responsive clinical support. Conduct virtual follow-up visits to support program onboarding, adjust care plans, reinforce medication adherence, and help patients progress toward lifestyle and health goals.

Document all clinical interactions accurately and efficiently, and prepare clear care summaries for patients’ primary care providers to ensure seamless coordination. Partner with interdisciplinary care teams to deliver high-quality, patient-centered care across chronic conditions such as CHF, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes.

Contribute to the development and refinement of clinical workflows and processes to support efficient, scalable, and high-impact care management programs. Represent Cadence ’s commitment to exceptional care in every patient interaction, aligning with the standards and goals of our health system partners.

What you'll need: Multi-state RN Compact State Licensure. Associate Degree in Nursing Science. 5+ years of recent clinical experience as an RN in anICU/ER setting is preferred. Prior experience supporting patients in a chronic care management program is a plus.

To ensure that our clinicians have the necessary tools for a successful remote work environment, home office setups must have consistently stable wifi with strong upload and download speeds. Excellent clinical acumen. Exceptional written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills. EMR experience, preferably in Athena and EPIC. Works effectively with minimum supervision. Strong collaboration with cross-functional partners.

Ability to support the delivery of health care to patients by performing a variety of activities and procedures that are prescribed by and performed under the direction of the Cadence Nurse Practitioner and Cadence clinical policies and procedures. Patient assessment competency.

Technical fluency with the ability to work in multiple platforms and systems, including Notion, Athena, EPIC, Zendesk, and G Suite. The anticipated base salary range for this role is $80,000 to $90,000 annual base salary , which is based on role scope, level, and location.

The CCICM RN Coordinator is administratively responsible for the clinical programming and daily operations of the CCICM initiative in alignment with VHA Directive 1110.04, Integrated Case Management Standards of Practice. The incumbent is responsible for the planning, development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of program operations.

The CCICM framework is a specialized, collaborative practice among multiple healthcare professions - it addresses physical, mental health and psychosocial needs to enhance Veterans' wellness, level of functioning, and quality of life.

The CCICM RN Coordinator implements standardized tools designed to bridge medical care and mental health care, transitioning inpatient care and outpatient care, and integrating community care and VA care for the Veteran.

The incumbent is based in the medical center in order to support real time, in person response to referrals, hands-on consultations/trainings, and education. In addition, the incumbent must be a skilled communicator capable of developing effective partnerships with CM staff, Service Line Chiefs and Executive Leadership.

Duties include, but are not limited to: -Serves as Richmond Virginia VA Medical Center's Care Coordination and Integrated Case Management (CCICM) Registered Nurse Coordinator, as a direct report to the Nursing Service. -Has expertise in coordinated care and serves as the integration liaison, alongside the CCICM Co-Champion for Social Work Service, between Executive Leadership and Case Management (CM) staff. -Manages the daily operations of the initiative and assists with ensuring facility-wide compliance with VHA Directive 1110.04 Integrated Case Management Standards of Practice. -Develops policies and procedures, monitors statistics and performance metrics, and prepares reports for facility, VISN, and national use. -Manages and controls the use of data related to CCICM day to day functioning and program evaluation.

In conjunction with the Case Management Supervisor, the RN Coordinator plans, organizes, and directs administrative, operational, patient and personnel activities for CCICM. -May be responsible for the program's budget, developing and monitoring staff compliance with practice, standards and guidelines on documentation, workload, data entry, ethical practice, and service delivery. -Provides analysis and evaluation of clinical program data and computerized programs to identify system-wide trends and needs to enhance the quality of service.

May be responsible for, or contribute to, the program's resource and fiscal management, monitoring control points developing the annual budget, operating within that budget, and accounting for appropriated funds. -Administratively responsible for the clinical programming and prepares reports and statistics for facility, VISN, and national use.

Will provide leadership, direction, orientation, coaching, in-service training, staff development, and continuing education programs for assigned staff. Will initiate and conduct a variety of program or service audits and complete designated clinical practice audits and reports, including productivity assessments.

Will oversee program operations and evaluations, identifying areas for improvement, gathering relevant data, assessing the data, developing, and implementing ideas for improvement and evaluating efficacy of improvement efforts. -Serves as a Lead Coordinator, a single, readily accessible, and clearly identifiable point of contact for a Servicemember or Veteran, his/her family and caregiver(s), and care team members.

Ensures Veteran care is coordinated across settings, services, and episodes of care, and the care plan is delivered as clinically indicated. Oversees care coordination and facilitates interprofessional team communications, reducing task and intervention duplication and improving the quality of care plan delivery.

Engages Veterans in self-management, self-determination, and shared decision making. -Performs other directly related duties as assigned.

## Company Description ##
Avec plus de 13'000 collaborateurs et collaboratrices représentant 160 métiers, les Hôpitaux Universitaires de Genève sont un établissement de référence au niveau national et international. Pour en savoir plus sur notre institution, prenez quelques minutes pour consulter notre rétrospective 2025 en cliquant ici.
Le Département de médecine de premier recours (DMPR) a pour mission sociétale de permettre un accès aux soins de qualité pour tous par une médecine de proximité, d-assurer la prise en charge des urgences médicales et chirurgicales légères, de promouvoir la prévention auprès des citoyennes et citoyens, d-apporter les connaissances médicales aux investigations judiciaires et de promouvoir la santé des voyageurs et voyageuses.
Le service de médecine tropicale et humanitaire assure la prise en charge de patients ayant voyagé et présentant une pathologie d-importation, tropicale ou parasitaire et prodigue des conseils de prévention. Il effectue des vaccinations spécialisées pour les voyageurs, les expatriés, les étudiants et la population locale. Par ailleurs, ce service participe activement aux interventions vaccinales en cas d-épidémie ou autre besoin identifié.
## Job Description ##
En qualité d-infirmier ou infirmière au Service de médecine tropicale et humanitaire (SMTH), votre mission consiste à mener de manière autonome des consultations infirmières de pré-voyage auprès d-une patientèle très diversifiée (expatriés, familles, humanitaires, immunosupprimés).
Vous menez et gérez des consultations infirmières de première ligne de manière autonome, dans le respect des missions, des protocoles et des délégations qui vous sont confiés.
Vous assurez également une activité de conseil aux voyageurs et voyageuses en formulant des recommandations personnalisées en matière de prévention des risques liés au voyage (vaccinations, prophylaxie, mesures d-hygiène, prévention des maladies infectieuses et autres risques sanitaires). Vous participez activement aux campagnes de vaccinations sur différents sites.
Vous travaillez en collaboration avec une équipe pluriprofessionnelle ainsi qu-avec les réseaux de soins internes et externes, notamment les organisations non gouvernementales, les organisations internationales et les partenaires présents au Global Health Campus.
Votre empathie, votre sens du relationnel et votre capacité à créer un climat de confiance vous permettent de vous positionner comme un partenaire de soins à part entière.
Doté ou dotée d-une excellente capacité d-adaptation et de l-organisation, vous êtes en mesure de faire face à des flux de patients importants et variables tout en maintenant une prise en charge de qualité. Vous gérez sereinement les imprévus et les situations génératrices de stress.
Vous possédez d-excellentes compétences relationnelles, un sens développé d l-accueil et une communication bienveillante, vous permettant de répondre aux attentes d-une patientèle exigeante et multiculturelle.
Dans le cadre de votre activité, vous êtes amené ou amenée à intervenir sur deux sites.

Vous possédez un Bachelor HES en soins infirmiers ou un diplôme en soins infirmiers équivalent reconnu par la Croix-Rouge suisse.
Vous avez une pratique professionnelle diversifiée de plus de 4 ans dans le domaine de la santé publique et/ou en santé communautaire et des connaissances en vaccinologie. Vous êtes au bénéfice d-une formation à l-évaluation clinique infirmière.
Une formation en médecine tropicale et des voyageurs constitue un réel atout.
Vous disposez d-un très bon niveau d-anglais, tant à l-oral qu-à l-écrit. La maitrise d-une autre langue, constitue un atout.
Vous savez vous adapter à divers contextes, aux imprévus, aux variations de charge de travail.
Vous possédez d-excellentes compétences relationnelles, un sens de l-accueil d-une communication bienveillante.

The Outpatient Behavioral Health (BH) Registered Nurse (RN) executes position responsibilities to improve Veteran and organizational outcomes.

The psychiatric BH RN executes their position duties by providing patient-centered, recovery-oriented principles, telemental health, community-based care, and self-awareness when caring for Veterans living with BH conditions.

The BH RN actively engages in interdisciplinary team huddles and meetings, uses therapeutic communication techniques, de-escalation practices, recovery-oriented language, and educates Veterans, their families, and significant others on illnesses, medications, and treatment plans.

The BH RN assists and/or directs safety concern resolution and collaborates with program leadership to help improve Veteran and program outcomes, liaising with Inpatient BH Units, develops content as well as facilitates nurse-led psychoeducational groups, and directs teams response to psychiatric and medical emergencies.

The BH RN documents assessments, risk screens, measurement-based care tools, clinical reminders, and Veteran care plans following facility policy, maintaining professional boundaries and acting in the Veteran's best interest.

The registered nurse (RN) assigned to the outpatient Behavioral Health team collaborates with interdisciplinary treatment teams in the delivery and coordination of comprehensive care to Veterans receiving outpatient behavioral health services.

The RN may work in, be assigned to, or provide cross-coverage for any Behavioral Health Service (BHS) program, Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs), or facility under the El Paso VA Health Care System based on patient care needs and operational requirements.

Assignments may include, but are not limited to, the Behavioral Health Access Team (BHAT), Primary Care Mental Health Integration (PCMHI), Behavioral Health Interdisciplinary Program (BHIP), Somatic Treatments (i.e Esketamine, etc.), Hospital Liaison, Intensive Community Mental Health Recovery (ICMHR), Housing and Urban Development-VA Supportive Housing (HUD-VASH).

The RN must maintain a current, valid, and unrestricted driver's license and possess the ability to safely operate a Government Services Administration (GSA) vehicle.

Driving responsibilities may include travel between CBOCs & Main VA Facility within the El Paso VA Health Care System, community-based and home visits, outreach activities, and minimal transportation of Veterans when necessary and consistent with VA policy and operational requirements.

This requirement supports the RN's responsibility to provide coverage and services across BHS programs, community settings, CBOCs, and other facilities that fall under the El Paso VA Health Care System.

Behavioral Health Services (BHS) provides a comprehensive range of services, including walk-in/same-day access, crisis assessment and management, group programming, evidence-based treatments, tele-mental health services, medication management, case management/Mental Health Treatment Coordinator (MHTC) services, counseling for couples and families, psychological assessment, outreach, and other behavioral health services.

The responsibilities of the Behavioral Health Registered Nurse (BH RN) include, but are not limited to, conducting risk assessments, triage, and clinical nursing services for Veterans seeking or receiving behavioral health care.

The BH RN addresses Secure Messaging (SM), Message Managers (MM), and other Veteran care requests within established facility policy and standards for timeliness, responding directly within the RN's scope of practice and appropriately routing, reassigning, or escalating requests to the appropriate team, provider, or service when indicated.

The RN reviews diagnostic and laboratory results, discusses abnormal findings with the referring or responsible provider, and communicates normal results to Veterans and/or caregivers, as appropriate. Other duties as assigned.

VA offers a comprehensive total rewards package: VA Nurse Total Rewards Pay: Competitive salary, regular salary increases, potential for performance awards Paid Time Off: 50 days of paid time off per year (26 days of annual leave, 13 days of sick leave, 11 paid Federal holidays per year) Retirement: Traditional federal pension (5 years vesting) and federal 401K with up to 5% in contributions by VA Insurance: Federal health/vision/dental/term life/long-term care (many federal insurance programs can be carried into retirement) Licensure: 1 full and unrestricted license from any US State or territory Work Schedule: Monday-Friday, 08:00am-04:45pm Telework: Available Ad Hoc Only Virtual: This is not a virtual position.
